title: A Pilot Study Using Gut-Directed Hypnotherapy for Hospitalized Patients
official: A Pilot Study Using Gut-Directed Hypnotherapy for Hospitalized Patients
summary: The purpose of the study is to compare the effectiveness of recorded gut-directed hypnosis to an educational recording in people with chronic problems in their gastrointestinal (GI) system. Patients who are hospitalized at Stanford Hospital for worsening pain and/or nausea will be considered for enrollment.

interventions.name: Gut directed hypnotherapy via telephone intervention

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults admitted to the GI inpatient service with expected length of stay \>24 hours
* Prior diagnosis of a disorder of gut-brain interaction, esophageal disorder, or inflammatory bowel disease
* Reason for hospitalization related to symptom management for exacerbation of visceral pain and/or nausea.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Currently using hypnosis
* severe developmental delay or cognitive impairment
* serious mental illness (i.e. psychosis or dissociation)
* hearing impairment
* Non-English speaking
* enrolled in another trial for GI symptom management
* admitted for GI procedure
